sentences.text: The petitioner is conducting a hotel within the territorial limits of the 1st respondent-Corporation.
The petitioner had obtained Exts.P2 license to run the hotel.
Before the expiry of the license, the petitioner has submitted Ext.P3 application for renewal of the same.
The petitioner has also submitted an application before the Pollution Control Board to renew the consent to operate.

While so, the 1st respondent issued Ext.P5 notice to the petitioner directing him to close down the hotel in light of the judgment in O.S.No.171/2021 passed by the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Ernakulam.

entities.text: Court of the Subordinate Judge, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner challenged Ext.P5 notice before this Court.
By Ext.P6 judgment, the 1st respondent has been directed to pass WP(C) NO. 21868 OF 2025 2025:KER:62290 orders on the application for renewal of the license.
In fact there is no necessity for the petitioner to obtain consent from the Pollution Control Board, since the hotel falls under the white category.
The petitioner produced Ext.P9 copy of the intimation of operation before the 2nd respondent and requested for renewal of the license.
But the 2nd respondent is insisting for an order from the Court to renew the license in light of the judgment in O.S.No.171/2021.
The stand of the 2 nd respondent is arbitrary.
Hence, the writ petition.
3. Heard; the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the respective Standing Counsel for the respondents 1 and 2, and 3.

Even though service of notice is complete on the respondents 4 to 6,
there is no appearance for them.

On a consideration of the facts and materials on record, especially that the petitioner's application for renewal of trade license is pending consideration before the 2nd respondent since 2023 onwards, without expressing anything on the merits of the matter, I direct the 2nd respondent to consider and dispose of the WP(C) NO. 21868 OF 2025 2025:KER:62290 application for renewal of license in accordance with law, and as expeditiously as possible, at any rate within 30 days from the date of production of a copy of this judgment after affording the petitioner and the respondents 4 to 6 an opportunity of being heard.
